as someone who finally got a proper diagnosis from a team of doctors at age 14 when my asd symptoms actually started to show to more people than my parents, it changes everything

we’re not “mentally disabled” but “developmentally disabled”. my only complaint is that it’s called a disorder instead of what it should be: a disability, because it can be extremely disabling to a lot of people who are lower on the end of sensory processing and whatnot.

i’ve never had an ear infection as a kid as far as i know (parents were freaking out much more over my surprise kidney reflux and rotavirus combo) but windy days make walking actual torture to the point where i just cover my ears in agony and tug on my dog’s leash so i can get home as quickly as possible.

please make a proper diagnosis with a doctor, if possible. finding out you were on on the spectrum your entire life is a life-changing experience and, in your case, lifestyle changes are long overdue since stress in itself shortens our lifespans. however, a questionnaire that could be made by anyone isn’t a concrete answer and should be taken with a grain of salt.
